title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act is a proposed law that aims to protect the integrity of elections by stopping the use of AI‑generated content that could mislead or manipulate voters. It would set up oversight rules, require transparency about AI tools used in campaign messaging, and impose penalties for spreading false AI‑created political information.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House says Congress should not give extra money or special regulatory help to AI firms or financial institutions that are in trouble because of stress in the AI market. Instead, Congress must provide assistance to all Americans who have been harmed.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 aims to ensure that all AI research is conducted in a trustworthy and safe manner by setting clear standards for reliability and transparency. The act establishes oversight mechanisms, reporting requirements, and accountability measures to prevent misuse and promote responsible innovation in AI technologies.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to disclose when and how artificial intelligence systems are used in services for veterans, ensuring that veterans and stakeholders understand AI’s role in decision‑making. It also mandates the VA to maintain public reports, provide explainable AI outputs, and establish oversight mechanisms to monitor compliance.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is a proposed law that would establish rules and oversight for how artificial intelligence is used to process veterans’ claims, ensuring that decisions are fair and can be explained. It aims to create transparency, protect veterans’ rights, and provide mechanisms for reviewing and correcting any AI-driven errors in claim adjudication.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is designed to safeguard consumers by preventing misleading or deceptive use of AI technologies. It establishes clear standards for transparency, accountability, and penalties to ensure AI systems do not misinform or exploit users.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is designed to strengthen protections around advanced artificial intelligence systems, ensuring they are built and deployed with robust security safeguards. It requires organizations to evaluate AI risks, implement mitigation strategies, and establish ongoing oversight to prevent misuse and safeguard public safety.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act proposes creating a dedicated task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to oversee the safe development, deployment, and regulation of artificial intelligence technologies across the United States. This act aims to establish clear guidelines, risk assessment protocols, and collaborative partnerships with industry and academia to protect critical infrastructure and national security from AI-related threats.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 is designed to create rules that help identify and reduce dangers from AI systems. It also requires companies to be transparent and secure in how they develop and use AI to protect people from potential harms.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 creates a national framework for regulating AI‑controlled machines and robots, requiring them to meet safety, transparency, and interoperability standards before they can be deployed. It also establishes a coordination body to oversee certification, manage liability, and promote collaboration among industry, government, and the public to ensure responsible use of these AI physical systems.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is designed to safeguard the integrity of electoral processes by preventing the use of artificial intelligence to mislead or manipulate voters. The law would likely require transparency, labeling, and restrictions on AI-generated political content to ensure that election-related information remains trustworthy and free from deception.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act requires developers to closely track and document any changes made by AI systems that can modify themselves, ensuring those changes do not pose safety or compliance risks. It establishes a framework for ongoing oversight, reporting, and regulation of self‑improving AI to protect public interests.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act would temporarily halt the construction of new data centers specifically for AI applications while authorities evaluate their environmental, security, and societal impacts. This pause allows time to develop and enforce stricter standards before any new AI data centers can open or expand operations.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is legislation designed to prevent the deployment of artificial intelligence systems that could act unpredictably or harmfully without proper oversight. It establishes regulatory safeguards, oversight mechanisms, and penalties to ensure AI technologies remain aligned with human values and safety standards.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board that will investigate cybersecurity incidents involving artificial intelligence and monitor compliance with AI safety standards. The board will also offer guidance and recommendations to improve AI security practices and help prevent future cyber threats.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act aims to guide the development and use of artificial intelligence so that it benefits the American public. It proposes policies to promote innovation, ensure fairness, and protect citizens’ privacy and safety as AI technologies advance.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act is a law that requires AI developers and companies operating in China to produce regular reports about the power consumption and energy usage of their AI systems. By mandating these disclosures, the act seeks to increase transparency, help manage environmental impact, and support regulatory oversight of AI development.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 prohibits artificial intelligence from acting as a primary medical provider, requiring that all diagnoses, treatment plans, and patient interactions be carried out by licensed human doctors. The law also mandates strict transparency and oversight for any AI tools used in healthcare, ensuring they are only used as assistive technologies under direct human supervision.

title: To establish the Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats within the Executive Office of the President, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This bill proposes creating a new Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats inside the Executive Office of the President. The office would monitor and mitigate risks from AI and other emerging technologies to protect national security and public welfare.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution proposes creating a Select Committee focused on artificial intelligence. The committee would be tasked with reviewing and guiding AI policy, regulation, and oversight.
